demonstration.description: The paper is a demonstration, a worked example or a teaching paper, whose data are synthetic: G1's finding of results quoted from a synthetic input is then information, and the submission pack's title page says the data are synthetic.

english_variant.description: British or American spelling, which G14 holds the manuscript to, and the language the build gives the document. The author's choice; a journal profile may ask for one. Absent, nothing is declared: G14 holds the paper to the English most of its words are in, the document is written as English with no region, and a date is printed day, month, year.

target_journal.description: Name of a profile under profiles/journals/. Absent means no journal chosen yet, which disables the journal gate rather than failing it.

study_type.description: The study's design. G12 asks the analysis plan for the sections this design needs beyond the seven every plan has, and G5 says where none of the reporting guidelines for it is declared. Each design's sections cite the guideline item they come from (src/manuscript_guard/data/study_types.yaml). Absent, the plan is asked for the seven only.

registration.description: The study's registrations. `manuscript-guard lookup --registrations` asks ClinicalTrials.gov, the EU PAS register, OSF and ISRCTN about each one and keeps the answer in design/registrations/; any other registry's record is copied by hand. G12 then holds the paper to it: the identifier is in the manuscript, the registry knows it, it was registered before the study started and before the first results, and each registered outcome quoted here is in the registry's record under the role given and is reported as the planned result named.

id.description: As the registry writes it: NCT04368728, EUPAS1000000417, ISRCTN17072692, osf.io/abcde, CRD42020123456.

registry.description: The registry's name, needed only where the identifier's shape does not say it: anzctr, drks, jrct. Its record is copied by hand into design/registrations/.

retrospective.description: Why the study was registered after it started, or after the first results were written. With it, and with the manuscript saying the study was registered retrospectively, G12 notes a late registration rather than failing it at submission.

outcomes.description: Each outcome the registration holds, quoted in the registry's words, with the role it has there and the planned result that reports it. One the paper does not report has no `reported_as`, and the plan's Deviations section quotes the same words.

registered.description: Words of the registered outcome, as the registry's record has them. Case, spacing and line breaks are not compared.

reported_as.description: The key of the result that reports it, as the plan's Planned results section lists it: `ror.point`, `results.dose`, or a group, `ror.*`.

reporting_guideline.description: Names of checklists under profiles/reporting/. Commonly STROBE, RECORD, RECORD-PE, CONSORT, SPIRIT, PRISMA, TRIPOD or ARRIVE, but deliberately not a closed list: guidelines are revised, extensions appear, and a schema that refuses CHEERS or SQUIRE would be wrong about the world rather than about the project.

custodian.description: What the custodian of the data forbids, as the data-use agreement says.

minimum_cell_count.description: The smallest count that may be published. A count the manuscript binds that is at least one and below it fails G2 from the internal-review stage.

restricts_sending.description: The custodian forbids sending the manuscript or its results anywhere they have not agreed to: `review --run` sends to a model the built-in Ollama runs on this machine, and to any other provider, one added at localhost included, only once the data custodian named in authors.yaml has authorised it with `manuscript-guard sign`.

package.description: What `manuscript-guard package` deposits besides the code and the results, and the deposit's DOI once it has one.

licence.description: The SPDX identifier of the licence the deposit is under, as CITATION.cff names it, or a list of them (code and data under two): `MIT`, `[MIT, CC-BY-4.0]`. The licence file itself is the project's LICENSE; the tool chooses none.

share.description: Inputs the analysis declared that may be deposited, each as its path in the results' provenance. An input declared synthetic goes without being listed; one declared restricted never goes, and listing it is refused. Every other input is withheld and listed in INPUTS.md.

request.description: How to obtain the inputs the package withholds: who to apply to, and on what terms. Required by `package` when it withholds any.

doi.description: The DOI of the deposited package, as the repository reserved or gave it, without the resolver. G4 warns while neither the Data availability statement nor a Code or Software availability statement names it, and fails at submission.

stage.description: How far along the work is. Every gate runs at every stage; the stage decides which findings fail rather than being reported as not yet due. A checker that demands everything from the first day is a checker that gets switched off on the second. Defaults to drafting.

rounds_required.description: Complete review rounds expected before a submission build. Two by default: the second panel is blinded to the first, because a panel that reads the earlier findings inherits their blind spots.

models.description: The models that read the panel's remits when `manuscript-guard review --run` is used, each as provider/model: [openai/<model>, mistral/<model>]. `manuscript-guard review --providers` lists the providers that are built in. Model names are the author's to supply; none is built in, because they change. API keys are not written here or anywhere: each provider's key is read from its environment variable.

providers.description: Providers that are not built in, by name. Each needs the base URL its chat endpoint sits under. A built-in name cannot be redefined.

base_url.description: https, or http for this machine only. Without a path beyond the API root: `/chat/completions` (or `/messages`) is added to it.

key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable that holds the key, never the key. Leave it out for a provider that takes none.

api.description: Which request shape the provider speaks: the chat API OpenAI defined, which most offer, or Anthropic's.

max_output_tokens.description: A cap on each reply. Unset, a provider's own default applies, except where its API requires a cap. A model that reasons before answering spends this on its reasoning first, and a reply cut short is refused.

paths.description: Overrides for the default layout. Every path is project-relative.

conventions.description: Project-specific additions to the shipped convention allowlist. Each needs a justification, because an allowlist that grows without argument eventually swallows the numbers it was meant to police.

id.description: A name for the convention. The report and `explain` cite the rule as `project:<id>`; without one, by the first 24 characters of its pattern.

terms.description: Project-specific tokens that contain digits but are names, not claims: CYP3A4, SARS-CoV-2, HbA1c.

lookup.description: How `manuscript-guard lookup` asks the registries for each cited reference's DOI and PMID, or searches them for one with neither. Keys are never written here: NCBI's is read from NCBI_API_KEY and OpenAlex's from OPENALEX_API_KEY.

contact.description: The address Crossref and NCBI ask a tool to give, so that they can write before they block it. MANUSCRIPT_GUARD_CONTACT in the environment is used in its place where set. It is sent with each request and never kept in a record.

max_age_days.description: How old a lookup record may be before G7 says so (`lookup-stale`, a warning): a work can be retracted after it is cited.

cited_as_retracted.description: References the paper cites knowing they are retracted, or that are themselves a retraction notice, each with the reason: a paper that discusses the retracted work, or cites the notice. G7 then notes them rather than failing.

not_indexed.description: References with no DOI and no PMID that are real and in no registry, each with the reason: an internal report, a regional journal, a work cited by a translated title. `lookup` does not search for them, and G7 notes them rather than saying no registry has them (`reference-not-found`).

displays.description: Tables and figures the journal gets as files of their own, which the text cites and does not place: a flow chart drawn by hand, a figure the journal asks for as a separate upload. G2 counts them with those placed by {{table.<key>}} and {{figure.<key>}}, so that a pointer to one is not a pointer to nothing.

language.description: How this paper's language is checked.

known_abbreviations.description: Short forms this paper uses without defining them, because the journal lets them stand or its readers take them for words or names: CI, PCR, MedDRA. Written as the manuscript writes them, and in quotes: unquoted, YAML reads NO, ON and YES as booleans. G14 reports any other abbreviation it finds used and not defined.

accepted_spellings.description: Single words this paper keeps although G14's list gives them to the other English: a field's own spelling, as orthopaedic is for American orthopaedics, or one word of a name. Letters only, in any case: a word is what G14 reads, so an entry with a space or a hyphen in it would match nothing. G14 reports any other word that is spelt the way english_variant does not spell it.

vocabulary.description: The terms this paper keeps to. Each entry names one term to use and the terms it replaces; G14 reports a replaced term the manuscript still uses, once, at its first use, with how many times it is used. A term is one word or several, matched whole, with a hyphen or a line break between its words and with its plural s; in any case, except for a word written with two capitals together, as OR, WHO and the II of phase II trial are, which is matched as written. Quote the terms: unquoted, YAML reads no, on and yes as booleans.

use.description: The term the manuscript uses for this thing. It holds a letter or a digit.

avoid.description: Other words for the same thing, which the manuscript does not use.

why.description: Why this term, for a co-author reading the file: the journal's wording, a reporting guideline's, the field's.
